title: NULL Pointer Dereference in wg_index_hashtable_lookup via entry->peer Overwrite
analysis:
In `wg_index_hashtable_lookup()`, when looking up an index entry (such as for an incoming data packet, cookie message, or handshake response), the code attempts to obtain a reference to the peer associated with the entry via `wg_peer_get_maybe_zero(entry->peer)`. However, instead of storing the returned reference into a local variable or into `*peer`, line 218 incorrectly assigns the return value directly back to `entry->peer`:
```c
entry->peer = wg_peer_get_maybe_zero(entry->peer);
```
When an incoming packet references an index associated with a peer that is being torn down (e.g., peer removal via netlink, session timeout, or interface shutdown), `peer->refcount` has already dropped to zero. In this case, `wg_peer_get_maybe_zero(entry->peer)` fails and returns `NULL`. As a result of the assignment, `entry->peer` is permanently overwritten with `NULL` within the `struct index_hashtable_entry` (which is embedded in `struct noise_keypair` or `struct noise_handshake`).

Subsequently, when the keypair is destroyed (or handshake is cleared), `keypair_free_kref()` (or `wg_noise_handshake_clear()`) executes:
```c
keypair->entry.peer->device->dev->name
wg_index_hashtable_remove(keypair->entry.peer->device->index_hashtable, &keypair->entry);
```
Since `keypair->entry.peer` was corrupted to `NULL`, dereferencing `keypair->entry.peer->device` results in an immediate kernel NULL pointer dereference panic, causing a remote denial of service (DoS).

Data Path:
- Source: Untrusted UDP packet received on the WireGuard listening socket (e.g., in `wg_packet_consume_data()`, `wg_cookie_message_consume()`, or `wg_noise_handshake_consume_response()`).
- Sanitization/Validation: None. Any validly formatted WireGuard packet header carrying an index matching a tearing-down peer will reach `wg_index_hashtable_lookup()`.
- Sink: Line 218 of `drivers/net/wireguard/peerlookup.c` overwriting `entry->peer` with NULL, subsequently dereferenced at `drivers/net/wireguard/noise.c:123` / `126`.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Send a WireGuard data packet (type 0x04) or handshake cookie message over UDP to the WireGuard port where `key_idx` is set to the receiver index of a keypair belonging to a peer that is being removed or expiring:
Packet bytes:
`04 00 00 00` (MESSAGE_DATA type = 4)
`<key_idx>` (4 bytes little-endian receiver index of the expiring peer)
`<counter>` (8 bytes arbitrary counter)
`<encrypted_data>` (arbitrary payload >= 16 bytes)
When received, `wg_packet_consume_data()` invokes `wg_index_hashtable_lookup()`, which sets `keypair->entry.peer = NULL`. Upon completion of peer cleanup, `keypair_free_kref()` triggers a kernel NULL pointer dereference crash.
